claim: Across 50,000 independent YouTube channels with documented 2019-2026 trajectories, CreatorMap reports median upload frequency of 4.53 videos per month for breakout channels versus 2.74 for growing and 1.52 for stalling channels, and a median longest hiatus of 35 days versus 81 and 200 days.
stance_target: Sustained posting cadence rather than audience engagement rate separates growing creators from stalling ones
scope_conditions: Vendor study, May 2026; the sample is conditioned on channels that survived to have a measurable 2019-2026 trajectory, so it says nothing about channels that exited; up to 50 recent videos per channel; all correlations are weak (absolute r no greater than 0.26) and the article explicitly disclaims coverage of thumbnails, titles, topic selection and production value
quoted_support: The longest gap between uploads correlates with subscriber growth at r = -0.26, the strongest correlation in our entire feature set. More plainly: channels that take long breaks grow the least.

claim: The CreatorMap growth study reports a positive correlation of r = +0.21 between schedule irregularity and subscriber growth while simultaneously reporting that breakout channels have the lowest irregularity, a sign contradiction its own charts do not resolve.
stance_target: The internal statistical coherence of CreatorMap's behavioural findings
scope_conditions: Same page, chart caption versus body text; the article also nominates three different variables as its 'strongest' predictor in three separate sections
quoted_support: Schedule irregularity (CV of upload gaps) by growth outcome - lower = more consistent ... Correlation with growth: r = +0.21.
